# Honest Weight Loss Reviews — full site text

> Independent reviews of behaviour-change weight-loss apps and meal plans for adults in the United States (18+). No promises about results, no testimonials, no invented figures. Every price and trial term is checked against official pages or labelled "To be verified".

## Home

https://wlreviews.github.io/

Positioning: "Weight-loss apps, reviewed the slow way." We compare behaviour-change apps and meal plans on price, method, and fit — checking every figure against the official page before we print it. No promises about results, no before-and-after stories, no invented reviews.

What we do: compare programs side by side, including a third option; check price, trial terms, and features against official pages before publishing; say plainly who a program may suit — and who it may not; label anything unverified as "To be verified" instead of guessing.

What we don't do: promise pounds lost or a timeframe for results; publish testimonials or before-and-after stories; recommend weight-loss products to anyone under 18; write about GLP-1 medication programs or weight-loss patches.

## Hub article: WeightWatchers vs Noom — an honest comparison

https://wlreviews.github.io/ww-vs-noom.html

Status: published 2026-11-20. Full text live, about 5,350 words, 18 FAQs. Prices and trial terms checked 20 November 2026 against official pages; WeightWatchers prices checked 27 November 2026.

Short answer: WeightWatchers and Noom are both behaviour-change programs, but they work differently. WeightWatchers is built around its Points system and workshops; Noom is built around short psychology-based lessons and food colour categories. MyFitnessPal is the third option: a tracker, not a program.

Verified prices: Noom $70 a month, or $169 for 4 months / $209 for 12 months paid up front, 7-day initial trial (checked 20 November 2026); WeightWatchers Core from $5 a month for the first month, then $10 a month, Core+ from $10 a month for the first month, then $20 a month (12-month plans; Black Friday offer ends 4 December 2026, checked 27 November 2026); MyFitnessPal Premium $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year, 7-day free trial (auto-renews unless cancelled), checked live 22 November 2026. MyFitnessPal prices changed between checks ($79.99 a year and $19.99 a month on 21 November 2026); Premium+ was not listed on the live page on 22 November 2026.

Sections: How we compare; What Noom is; What WeightWatchers is; What MyFitnessPal is, and why it is here; Price and free trial; What a typical day looks like; Who each program may suit — and who it may not; Strengths and weaknesses; Common objections, answered; Our recommendation (published, with the recommended program's weaknesses named).

Frequently asked questions: 18, covering price, trial, cancellation, exercise, food colour system, and which program fits which reader.

## Noom vs MyFitnessPal: Behavior Change or Calorie Counting?

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-vs-myfitnesspal.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 4,310 words, 8 FAQs. Prices and trial terms checked 22 November 2026 against official pages.

Short answer: Noom and MyFitnessPal solve different problems. Noom is a behaviour-change program: daily psychology lessons, a colour-coded food system, and a goal coach, for $70 a month or $209 a year paid up front. MyFitnessPal is a calorie-counting tracker: log food with barcode or voice search, track macros, and log exercise, with a free version and Premium at $49.99 a year.

Verified prices (22 November 2026): Noom $70 a month, or $169 for 4 months / $209 for 12 months paid up front, 7-day initial trial; MyFitnessPal Premium $49.99 a year or $9.99 a month, 7-day free trial (auto-renews unless cancelled). MyFitnessPal prices changed between checks ($79.99 a year and $19.99 a month on 21 November 2026); Premium+ was not listed on the live page on 22 November 2026.

Sections: Noom vs MyFitnessPal at a glance; The core difference: behaviour change vs calorie counting; How Noom works; How MyFitnessPal works; Food tracking compared; Coaching and support; Price compared; Free trials compared; Who each one suits — and who it does not; Strengths and weaknesses; Common objections, answered; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (8); Sources.

Still to be verified (labelled in the article): Noom trial fee (if any) and whether the trial requires a card; exact cancellation steps for Noom; coach reply speed and whether coaching is one-to-one.

## Can You Use Noom Without Exercise? What It Requires

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-without-exercise.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 2,512 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 22 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Yes. Noom does not require exercise. It starts with food — exercise is something you add when you are ready, starting with 200 steps a day. There is no gym requirement, no workout plan, and no exercise target you must hit. What Noom asks of you every day is a short lesson of 5–15 minutes, logging everything you eat, and — if you want — a daily weigh-in and a check-in with your coach.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): exercise tracking starts with 200 steps a day (app includes a pedometer), building up as confidence builds; food comes first; daily lessons 5–15 minutes based on CBT; plan usually around 16 weeks; 7-day initial trial; $70 a month or $209 for 12 months paid up front; food colours green, yellow, orange; syncs with Apple Watch, Fitbit, and Garmin (plus iHealth, Misfit, Omron, Polar, Qardio, Runkeeper, Withings, Yoo); tracks weight, water intake, glucose levels, and blood pressure.

Sections: What Noom actually asks you to do every day; What Noom says about exercise; What a day without exercise looks like; When exercise does enter the picture; Who this suits — and who it may not; Common objections, answered; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

Still to be verified (labelled in the article): Noom trial fee (if any) and whether the trial requires a card; exact cancellation steps for Noom; how quickly a Noom coach replies and whether coaching is one-to-one; Noom does not publish a specific exercise target beyond starting at 200 steps a day.

Affiliate links: none on this page (stated in the article and footer).

## Noom Food Color System: Green, Yellow, and Orange Explained

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-food-color-system.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 2,543 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 22 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Noom sorts every food you log into green, yellow, or orange by calorie density — not good or bad. Green is about 30% of daily intake, yellow about 45%, orange about 25%, and no food is off limits.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): colours are green/yellow/orange (not red); green is the least calorie-dense (most vegetables, some fruits, whole grains); yellow is the largest share (lean meats, starches, avocados, legumes); orange is the most calorie-dense and/or has the fewest nutrients (cheeseburgers, desserts); "orange doesn't mean bad"; the tracker tells you the colour when you log; suggested daily allotment for each colour; half a pound of peanut butter 1,334 calories vs half a pound of spinach 52; half a pound of oatmeal 154 calories and green because of fiber.

Sections: What the colors actually mean; Green: about 30%; Yellow: about 45%; Orange: about 25%; How the system works when you log; What the colors do not mean; Common mistakes; How this fits the rest of Noom; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

Still to be verified (labelled in the article): Noom trial fee (if any) and whether the trial requires a card; exact cancellation steps for Noom; how quickly a Noom coach replies and whether coaching is one-to-one; the official pages give examples for each color, not complete food lists — the tracker assigns the color when you log.

Affiliate links: none on this page (stated in the article and footer).

## What Is Noom Behavior Change? CBT Lessons Explained

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-behavior-change.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 2,689 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 22 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Behavior change in Noom means changing how you think and feel about eating, not just what you eat. Daily lessons of 5–15 minutes, based on cognitive behavioral therapy, teach you to spot triggers, handle emotional and stress eating, tell genuine hunger from "head hunger," and manage plateaus. Not a fad diet, no banned foods, no pre-packaged meals.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): psychology-based approach, "weight loss isn't just about what you eat, but why you eat"; sustainable habits for a lifetime; step-by-step changes; daily lessons around 5–15 minutes from day one, with exercises, quizzes, or tasks; seven lesson topics named on Noom's page (triggers; emotional and stress eating; what to do instead of reaching for a snack; mindfulness; choosing filling foods; genuine hunger vs "head hunger"; managing plateaus); lessons based on CBT, "a type of therapy that's been proven to help people change their habits and behavior", "gold standard in behavioral science"; Noom does not believe in losing weight through sheer willpower or by restricting foods; not a fad diet or an elimination diet; plan usually around 16 weeks; 7-day initial trial; $70 a month or $209 for 12 months.

Sections: What "behavior change" means here; The daily lessons: what they actually teach; CBT, in plain terms; What a lesson looks like in a day; What behavior change does not mean; Who this suits — and who it may not; Common objections, answered; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

Still to be verified (labelled in the article): Noom trial fee (if any) and whether the trial requires a card; exact cancellation steps for Noom; how quickly a Noom coach replies and whether coaching is one-to-one; Noom does not publish the full lesson curriculum — the topics listed here are the ones named on its official pages.

Affiliate links: none on this page (stated in the article and footer).

## What Does a Noom Coach Do? Support, Check-Ins, Limits

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-coaching.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 2,383 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 22 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: A Noom coach supports you every step of the way: looking at your food log and suggesting different foods to try, and helping you stay motivated when you feel stuck — including through plateaus. Coaching is included at no extra cost. Coaches adapt to your needs: checking in once every couple of weeks is fine, or more often if you need it. They are trained in the science behind behavior change.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): "Your Noom coach is there to support you every step of the way with high fives and helpful tips"; coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods; help you stay motivated when stuck, plateau named; coaches adapt to your needs, check-in once every couple of weeks is fine; you can reach out to your goal coach when you need one; coaches "trained in the science behind behavior change"; group of Noomers for inspiration, advice, or to share your wins; Noom's comparison table describes its coaching as "coaching at no extra cost"; $70 a month or $209 for 12 months; 7-day initial trial.

Sections: What the coach actually does; How check-ins work; What the coach is trained in; Coaching and community; What coaching is not; Who coaching helps most — and who may not need it; Common objections, answered; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

## Noom Monthly vs Annual Plans: Which One Costs Less?

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-monthly-vs-annual.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 2,089 words, 6 FAQs. Prices checked 22 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: The annual plan is cheapest per month at $17.40, paid as $209 up front. Month-to-month is $70 a month. The 4-month plan most people pick is $169 up front, $42.25 a month. All plans are prepaid and auto-renew. The cheapest plan is only cheapest if you use it.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): all 12 plan prices ($70 / $129 / $159 / $169 / $174 / $179 / $184 / $189 / $195 / $199 / $205 / $209); monthly averages are the plan price divided by its length (our arithmetic), except $70, $42.25, and $17.40 which Noom itself states; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; all plans billed up front and auto-renew; plan usually around 16 weeks; 7-day initial trial. Savings by arithmetic: 12 months $840 vs $209 = $631; 4 months $280 vs $169 = $111; 6 months $420 vs $179 = $241.

## How Noom Food Logging Works: What a Day Looks Like

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-food-logging.html

Status: published 2026-11-22. Full text live, about 2,410 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 22 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Log everything you eat — after each meal and snack, or at the end of the day, your choice. Every food you log gets a color: green, yellow, or orange by calorie density, with a suggested daily allotment for each. Your coach can see the log and suggest foods. Weighing in daily is optional.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): logging everything is a key element of the program; log after each meal and snack or at the end of the day; the tracker tells you the color of every food you log; a suggested daily allotment for each color; the program works within a daily calorie range; over time you learn to fill up on more green and yellow foods; coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods; coaches adapt, checking in once every couple of weeks is fine; a group of Noomers for inspiration, advice, or to share wins; recipe database of thousands with "how green" information and caloric range fit; daily lessons 5–15 minutes; plan usually around 16 weeks; 7-day trial; daily weigh-ins reduce anxiety about the scale, weight fluctuations are normal, graph won't be a straight line, daily weigh-in is an option on the main page.

Worth it if you want structure and a coach and will use it for 16 weeks; not worth it if you want a set meal plan or the cheapest tracker.

Verified facts (22 November 2026): Noom 12 plans $70–$209, monthly $70, 4-month $169 ($42.25 a month), annual $209 ($17.40 a month), all billed up front and auto-renewing, 7-day initial trial; MyFitnessPal Premium Annual $49.99 a year, Monthly $9.99 a month, 58% savings on the annual plan, free version with basic tracking, Premium adds barcode and voice logging, custom macros, ad-free, meal scan, intermittent fasting, food insights, no Premium+ on the page; MFP 7-day free trial for first-time users, first charge at trial end unless cancelled, auto-renew, cancel via Settings / App Store / Google Play. Arithmetic: $209 − $49.99 = $159.01; $49.99 ÷ $209 ≈ 24%; $70 − $9.99 = $60.01; 12 months monthly billing $840 vs $119.88, difference $720.12; $209 ÷ $49.99 = 4.18; $70 ÷ $9.99 = 7.01; $49.99 ÷ 12 = $4.17. MFP $49.99 verified by two live-browser reads; text crawls the same day showed $79.99 — a coherent stale set ($79.99/year, $19.99/month, 67%) matching the 20–21 November old prices (see proof-kb open-questions.md).

## Noom Daily Lessons: What You Learn Each Day 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-daily-lessons.html

Status: published 2026-11-23. Full text live, about 2,200 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 23 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Noom gives you a short lesson every day from day one. Each takes around 5–15 minutes, is built on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and gives you exercises, quizzes or tasks to complete. The lessons cover seven things Noom says you will learn — your triggers, emotional and stress eating, what to do instead of snacking, mindfulness, choosing foods, genuine hunger versus "head hunger", and plateaus. They sit in the same app as your food log. A plan usually runs for around 16 weeks.

Verified facts (23 November 2026): daily lessons from day 1, around 5–15 minutes (a second official page describes them as less than 15 minutes per day); each lesson gives exercises, quizzes or tasks to complete, plus insights into the root causes of eating habits; lessons based on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), described on the pages as the gold standard in behavioral science; seven topics you will learn (triggers, emotional and stress eating, what to do instead of reaching for a snack, mindfulness while eating, choosing foods, genuine hunger versus "head hunger", plateaus); lessons in the same app used to log food; plan usually around 16 weeks, but it can be more or less depending on your goal; log everything after each meal and snack or at the end of the day, tracker tells the color of every food; daily weigh-in is an option, not a requirement; coaches adapt to your needs, check in once every couple of weeks or more often; lessons included in every plan, $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan, $17.40 a month on the annual plan; 7-day initial trial. The pages do not say which day covers which topic, what time of day to read the lesson, or in what order to do the day's parts — the article lists the seven topics as themes, not a syllabus, and does not invent a timetable.

Sections: What a daily lesson is; What you learn: seven topics; How a lesson fits into your day; What the lessons do not do; Who the lessons suit, and who they do not suit; What the lessons cost; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

## Noom for Emotional Eaters: What the Lessons Teach 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-for-emotional-eating.html

Status: published 2026-11-23. Full text live, about 2,305 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 23 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Noom's lessons address emotional eating directly. Three of the seven things the program teaches speak to it — triggers, emotional and stress eating, and what to do instead of snacking. Two more support them: mindfulness, and telling genuine hunger from "head hunger". The lessons take around 5–15 minutes a day, are based on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and sit in the same app as your food log. The lessons are not therapy. A plan usually runs for around 16 weeks.

Verified facts (23 November 2026): three of the seven things you will learn speak directly to emotional eating (what triggers you to eat when you are not hungry, how to overcome emotional and stress eating, what to do instead of reaching for a snack when you do not feel good); two more support them (mindfulness while eating, telling genuine hunger from "head hunger"); Noom's list of who the program fits includes people who want to learn what to do besides reaching for food when they feel stressed, emotional, anxious, or bored, people who have tried weight-loss programs and not kept the weight off, and people who want a structured program with daily tasks; daily lessons from day 1, around 5–15 minutes (a second official page describes them as less than 15 minutes per day), exercises, quizzes or tasks to complete, insights into the root causes of eating habits; lessons based on CBT, described on the pages as the gold standard in behavioral science; coaches trained in the science behind behavior change, adapt to your needs, check in once every couple of weeks or more often, help when you hit a plateau; log everything after each meal and snack or at the end of the day, tracker tells the color of every food; daily weigh-in is an option, not a requirement, and daily weigh-ins help you see that small, temporary gains and losses are normal; lessons included in every plan, $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan, $17.40 a month on the annual plan; 7-day initial trial; plan usually around 16 weeks. The pages do not say which day covers which topic, what time of day to read the lesson, or in what order to do the day's parts; the pages do not describe Noom as treatment for an eating disorder, and this guide does not present it as one.

Sections: What Noom means by emotional eating; The three lessons that speak to it directly; The two supporting topics; How it works in a day; What the lessons do not do; Who it suits, and who it does not suit; What it costs; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

## Noom for Busy Professionals: What It Asks of You 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-for-busy-professionals.html

Status: published 2026-11-23. Full text live, about 2,124 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 23 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Noom asks a busy person for four things a day: a lesson of around 5–15 minutes, logging everything you eat after each meal or at the end of the day, a daily weigh-in if you want one, and movement starting at 200 steps. The lessons and the log live in the same app, and the coach checks in once every couple of weeks, or more often if you are struggling. The pages do not prescribe a time of day for any of it. A plan usually runs for around 16 weeks.

Verified facts (23 November 2026): one timed daily commitment — the lesson, around 5–15 minutes (a second official page describes the lessons as less than 15 minutes per day); the sign-up questions take about 10 minutes, once; lessons from day 1, based on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT); log everything after each meal and snack, or at the end of the day — your choice; the tracker tells the color of every food you log; the coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods to try; coaches adapt to your needs, check in once every couple of weeks or more often if you are struggling; daily weigh-in is an option, not a requirement, and daily weigh-ins help you see that small, temporary gains and losses are normal; exercise is encouraged but not required, starting at 200 steps a day — the page's example is 200 steps, then 400, then 1,000, an example of building up, not a prescribed ladder; Noom syncs with Apple Watch, Fitbit, and Garmin; the pages do not prescribe a time of day for the lesson, the log, or the weigh-in; plan usually around 16 weeks, but it can be more or less depending on your goal; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; lessons included in every plan, $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan, $17.40 a month on the annual plan; 7-day initial trial. The pages do not say how long logging takes, how long a weigh-in takes, how much time the coach takes, whether lessons work offline, whether you can re-read, skip, or catch up on a missed lesson, or how quickly a coach replies.

## Noom for People Who Have Tried Diets Before 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-for-people-who-tried-diets.html

Status: published 2026-11-23. Full text live, about 2,087 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 23 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Noom's answer to past diets is not another set of rules. It is a different approach: daily lessons built on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), a coach, and a color system for food — no food off limits, no willpower, no set meal plan. The lessons teach you the why behind how you eat: triggers, emotional and stress eating, and what to do instead of snacking. Noom says the program usually runs for around 16 weeks, and the pages give no outcome figures for people who have tried diets before.

Verified facts (23 November 2026): the pages' "Is Noom right for you?" list names people who have tried weight-loss programs in the past but have not been able to keep the weight off, people who want a different approach to weight loss that is sustainable and will lead to lasting change, and people who want a more structured program with daily tasks, challenges and lessons to keep them on track; a second official page adds that the program aims to help you sustain the healthy habits you develop and avoid yo-yo dieting; daily lessons from day 1, around 5–15 minutes, exercises, quizzes or tasks to complete, based on CBT; seven topics you will learn (triggers, emotional and stress eating, what to do instead of reaching for a snack, mindfulness while eating, choosing foods, genuine hunger versus "head hunger", plateaus); no willpower, no food restrictions; colors green/yellow/orange by calorie density, roughly 30/45/25, no food off limits; no set meal plan — daily calorie range, color system, recipe database, coach; coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods, checks in once every couple of weeks or more often if you are struggling, helps when you hit a plateau; log everything after each meal and snack or at the end of the day; daily weigh-in is an option, not a requirement; lessons, coach, and colors included in every plan, $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan, $17.40 a month on the annual plan; 7-day initial trial; plan usually around 16 weeks. The pages give no outcome figures for people who have tried diets before, compare no success rates with other programs, describe no separate track for repeat dieters, say nothing about why past diets stopped working, and do not describe Noom as a quick fix.

Sections: What "tried diets before" means on Noom's pages; What is different; What is the same; What the pages do not say; Who it suits, and who it does not suit; What it costs; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

## Noom for Vegetarians: How the Colors Work 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-for-vegetarians.html

Status: published 2026-11-23. Full text live, about 1,958 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 23 November 2026 against Noom's official pages.

Short answer: Noom works the same way for vegetarians. The color system sorts food by calorie density, not by whether it comes from animals: green foods include vegetables and whole grains, yellow includes starches and healthy fats, and orange is the highest density. No food is off limits, and there is no separate vegetarian plan — the lessons, the coach, and the log are the same for everyone. The pages do not list a vegetarian meal plan, and Noom gives no separate price for vegetarians.

Verified facts (23 November 2026): the pages do not use the word "vegetarian" in the passages checked; they say the program works the same way whether you are vegan, following a low-carb or keto diet, or are an intermittent faster; colors sort food by calorie density — green is the lowest, yellow is higher, orange is the highest, and orange does not mean "bad"; green is about 30% (vegetables, whole grains), yellow is about 45% (lean meats, starches, healthy fats like avocados and legumes), orange is about 25% (cheeseburgers, desserts); the tracker tells you the color of every food you log; Noom has a database of thousands of recipes with "how green" information; daily lessons from day 1, around 5–15 minutes, exercises, quizzes or tasks to complete, based on CBT; seven topics you will learn (triggers, emotional and stress eating, what to do instead of reaching for a snack, mindfulness while eating, choosing foods, genuine hunger versus "head hunger", plateaus); no willpower, no food restrictions; no set meal plan — daily calorie range, color system, recipe database, coach; coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods, checks in once every couple of weeks or more often if you are struggling, helps when you hit a plateau; log everything after each meal and snack or at the end of the day; daily weigh-in is an option, not a requirement; lessons, coach, and colors included in every plan, $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan, $17.40 a month on the annual plan; 7-day initial trial; plan usually around 16 weeks. The pages do not name the colors of tofu, lentils, eggs, or cheese on its own, do not say whether the recipe database filters for vegetarian recipes, do not say whether the coach suggests vegetarian foods specifically, and describe no separate vegetarian plan or vegetarian version of the lessons.

Sections: What the pages actually say; How the colors work for a vegetarian plate; What does not change; What the pages do not say; Who it suits, and who it does not suit; What it costs; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

## Noom vs WeightWatchers Cost: Which Is Cheaper? 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-vs-weightwatchers-cost.html

Status: published 2026-11-27. Full text live, about 2,207 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 27 November 2026 against Noom's and WeightWatchers' official pages.

Short answer: WeightWatchers Core is cheaper than Noom on price: $5 for the first month, then $10 a month on a 12-month plan, $115 in the first year, against Noom's $209 a year. Core auto-renews yearly at $10 a month ($120 a year). Noom's cheapest monthly average is $17.40 a month on its annual plan, and $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan most users take. But the prices buy different things: Noom includes daily CBT lessons, a coach, and the color system; WeightWatchers Core is built on the Points system, with nutrition guidance and recipes and a two-week trial of Workshops. The Core+ plan is $10 for the first month, then $20 a month, with the offer ending 4 December 2026 and auto-renewal at $20 a month.

Verified facts (27 November 2026): Noom $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; $17.40 a month on the annual plan and $42.25 a month on the 4-month plan, both as Noom states; 7-day initial trial; plan usually around 16 weeks; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; daily CBT lessons around 5–15 minutes from day 1; coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods, checks in once every couple of weeks or more often; colors green/yellow/orange roughly 30/45/25, no food off limits; no set meal plan; log everything; daily weigh-in is an option; plans prepaid and auto-renew. WeightWatchers Core $5 a month for the first month, then $10 a month on a 12-month plan, auto-renews yearly at $10 a month; Core+ $10 a month for the first month, then $20 a month, auto-renews yearly at $20 a month; both offers end 4 December 2026 (Black Friday offer; previous offer ended 26 November 2026); the page banner reads "BLACK FRIDAY SALE: Plans start at just $5 for your first month!"; Med+ $25 a month for the first three months, then $74 a month standard price; Core is built on the Points system; nutrition guidance and recipes including a recipe library of over 12,000 recipes (checked 20 November 2026); Core includes a two-week trial of Workshops when you purchase a Core membership; unlimited Workshops and unlimited Fitness Content are Core+ features, not Core.

Arithmetic (all our calculations, shown in the article): $5 + 11 × $10 = $115 in the first year; $209 − $115 = $94 a year; $5 + 3 × $10 = $35 for four months; $169 − $35 = $134; 12 × $10 = $120 a year on renewal; $209 − $120 = $89 a year; $70 ÷ $10 = 7; $17.40 − $10 = $7.40 a month; $10 + 11 × $20 = $230 in the first year; $230 − $209 = $21 a year; 12 × $20 = $240 a year on renewal; $240 − $209 = $31 a year.

Sections: The numbers side by side (table); The same four months, and the same year; What each price buys; Renewals and trials; Who it suits, and who it does not suit; What it costs; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

Still to be verified (labelled in the article): whether WeightWatchers Core includes access to Registered Dietitians; whether the Core plan itself has a free trial; Noom trial fee (if any) and whether the trial requires a card; exact cancellation steps for Noom; refund policy if you cancel a Noom plan mid-plan; how quickly a Noom coach replies and whether coaching is one-to-one.

Affiliate links: none on this page (stated in the article and footer).

## Noom vs MyFitnessPal: Free Trial and Features Compared 2026

https://wlreviews.github.io/noom-vs-myfitnesspal-free-trial.html

Status: published 2026-11-23. Full text live, about 2,299 words, 6 FAQs. Facts checked 23 November 2026 against Noom's and MyFitnessPal's official pages.

Short answer: Both trials last 7 days, and they work differently. Noom's 7-day initial trial starts your plan — daily CBT lessons, a coach, and the color system — and Noom calls it "no risk", but the pages do not say whether it costs anything or requires a card. MyFitnessPal's 7-day free trial gives first-time users Premium, and it auto-renews and charges your card when it ends unless you cancel first. Noom costs $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, or $209 a year; MyFitnessPal Premium costs $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year. For adults 18 and over only.

Verified facts (23 November 2026): Noom 7-day initial trial, called "no risk", starts the plan; daily CBT lessons around 5–15 minutes from day 1; coach can look at your food log and suggest different foods, checks in once every couple of weeks or more often; colors green/yellow/orange roughly 30/45/25, no food off limits; log everything; daily weigh-in is an option; recipe database of thousands with "how green" information; $70 a month, $169 for 4 months, $209 a year; most Noom Weight users have a 4-month subscription; plans prepaid and auto-renew. MyFitnessPal 7-day free trial only for people who have never upgraded to Premium and never started a Premium trial (checked live 22 November 2026); trial ends with the first payment charged to the card unless cancelled first, auto-renews, cancel in Settings or in the App Store or Google Play settings, Premium kept until the end of the current period (checked live 22 November 2026); Premium adds barcode scan and meal scan, voice log, macro tracking with custom goals, ad-free logging, intermittent fasting, and food insights and comparison; the free account already includes nutrition and weight tracking and exercise tracking (checked 23 November 2026); Premium $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year (checked live 22 November 2026). MyFitnessPal describes Premium as "like having a dietitian and trainer at your fingertips" — marketing language, not a coaching service.

MyFitnessPal prices: a text crawl on 23 November 2026 showed $79.99 a year, an older cached figure (third such crawl; the first two were 22 November 2026 at 02:31 and 03:50 UTC); the live page checked on 22 November 2026 showed $49.99 a year and $9.99 a month. If the live page shows $79.99 again, treat the price as unstable and record both readings with their times.

Sections: The two trials side by side (table); What the Noom trial gives you; What the MyFitnessPal trial gives you; Features compared (table); What it costs after the trial; Who it suits, and who it does not suit; Our verdict; Frequently asked questions (6); Sources.

Still to be verified (labelled in the article): whether the Noom trial costs anything and whether it requires a card; the exact cancellation steps for Noom; the refund policy if you cancel a Noom plan mid-plan; whether the Noom app scans barcodes; how quickly a Noom coach replies and whether coaching is one-to-one; MyFitnessPal prices (see the note above).
